text: By 2050, many experts believe we will have created Artificial General Intelligence, or AGI. Unlike today’s AI, which excels at single tasks, AGI would match human flexibility across any intellectual field. The potential benefits are enormous: personalized education, instant scientific discoveries, and solutions to climate change. However, the risks are equally serious. If we program AGI with flawed goals, it could act unpredictably, even harming people while trying to help. Timeline predictions vary wildly—some say 2030, others say never. The key, most researchers agree, is to build safety checks before we switch it on. We must slow down, test carefully, and decide together what values we want this powerful mind to follow.
